WHY_I_FIT:
Category and operations management is about one thing: getting the right product to the right place at the right cost, and doing it consistently. I have done exactly that.

When I founded **Naraina Jewellers**, I personally traveled to **Surat diamond cutting factories**, **Mumbai Zaveri Bazaar bullion houses**, and **Delhi wholesale markets** to build a sourcing network from zero. I evaluated **5+ manufacturing hubs**, negotiated **12+ vendor agreements** with direct factory MOQs (bypassing middlemen), and modeled a **Rs 25L+ working capital** budget covering inventory, store renovation, and seasonal turnover.

This was not a case study. I picked the retail store location by analyzing footfall patterns and competitor density. I finalized the brand name and visual identity. I managed store renovation contractors. I structured **GST registrations** and trade licensing. Every operational decision had a direct P&L consequence because it was my capital at risk.

Before that, at **Gandhi & Co.**, I managed **50+ active matters** simultaneously with zero deadline defaults, negotiated **15+ commercial agreements**, and coordinated workflows across multiple stakeholders with competing priorities. My MBA from **IIM Sirmaur** trained me in unit economics, financial statement analysis, and quantitative problem solving. I score in the **top 98.66%** on quantitative aptitude.

I bring the rare combination of genuine founder operations experience, structured contract negotiation skills, financial modeling proficiency in **MS Excel and Tally**, and the analytical rigor of an IIM MBA.
